exposure: Delivering a baby with epidermolysis bullosa
Mode of birth (Normal Vaginal Delivery vs. Caesarean Section)
cohort: The study included 195 responding obstetricians, 75 unaffected mothers who delivered EB babies, and 44 mothers with various types of EB.
finding: Most patients with epidermolysis bullosa (EB) who are capable of giving birth do not have an increased risk for pregnancy-related complications.
mod_finding: Normal vaginal delivery appears to be safe for mothers with EB, and there was no significant difference in blistering at birth in babies delivered via NVD compared to CS in either group.
